definitions.explanation: Paper manufactured using Western methods, as opposed to traditional Japanese washi. The standard paper used for printing, writing, and everyday purposes.

examples.japanese: {洋紙|ようし}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{和紙|わし}→和紙：02268_washi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{違|ちが}い→違い：03432_chigai⟧。
examples.english: The difference between Western paper and washi.

examples.japanese: ⟦{明治|めいじ}{時代|じだい}→明治時代：28080_meijijidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{洋紙|ようし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{製造|せいぞう}→製造：03289_seizou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{始|はじ}まった→始まる：00841_hajimaru⟧。
examples.english: Western-style paper manufacturing began in the Meiji period.

examples.japanese: ⟦{現在|げんざい}→現在：01556_genzai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{使|つか}われている→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦{紙|かみ}→紙：00712_kami⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ほとんど→ほとんど：00847_hotondo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{洋紙|ようし}だ。
examples.english: Most of the paper used in modern Japan is Western-style paper.

notes:
{洋紙|ようし} is the technical term for Western-style machine-made paper, as opposed to traditional Japanese ⟦{和紙|わし}→和紙：02268_washi⟧.

FORMS:
⟦{洋|よう}→洋：28890_you⟧ (Western) + {紙|し} (paper)

USAGE:
In everyday conversation, people simply say ⟦{紙|かみ}→紙：00712_kami⟧ since Western paper is the default. {洋紙|ようし} is mainly used when specifically contrasting with ⟦{和紙|わし}→和紙：02268_washi⟧, or in technical and industrial contexts.
Do not confuse with the homophone ⟦{用紙|ようし}→用紙：09588_youshi⟧ (paper/form for a specific purpose), which is far more common in daily life.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{和紙|わし}→和紙：02268_washi⟧: Japanese paper — traditional handmade paper from plant fibers like {楮|こうぞ}
- ⟦{紙|かみ}→紙：00712_kami⟧: paper — the general everyday word
- ⟦{用紙|ようし}→用紙：09588_youshi⟧: a form or sheet of paper (different kanji, same reading)
